benefit.name: Accessible Parking Permit (SPARC BC)
benefit.amount: Fees are set by SPARC BC; confirm the current fee on their site. Permanent permits are valid 3 years; temporary permits are valid 1-12 months and are not renewable.
benefit.summary: BC's accessible parking placard for people with mobility limitations. Hang it from the rear-view mirror. It is valid whether you drive or ride as a passenger.
benefit.requiresNote: Mobility limitation confirmed by a medical professional — for example you use a wheelchair or a mobility aid like a cane or crutches, or your health prevents you from walking far. You don't need to own a vehicle.
benefit.note: SPARC BC is the non-profit that runs BC's permit program. SPARC BC sets the fees. Check the current fee and any hardship help on its site.

detail.about: SPARC BC issues the accessible parking permits recognized in designated spaces across British Columbia. Two types exist: permanent (valid 3 years, renewable) and temporary (1 to 12 months, not renewable — reapply if still needed). The permit belongs to the person, not a car, and must be displayed on the rear-view mirror while parked.

aboutList.lead: SPARC BC issues the accessible parking permits recognized in designated spaces across British Columbia.
items: Two types exist: permanent (valid 3 years, renewable) and temporary (1 to 12 months, not renewable — reapply if still needed).
The permit belongs to the person, not a car, and must be displayed on the rear-view mirror while parked.

steps: Download the application form from sparc.bc.ca or call 604-718-7744 / 1-888-718-7794 for a copy
Have the referral section completed by a medical professional with a valid MSP number
Check SPARC BC's site for the current fee and submit it with the application; ask about hardship assistance if needed
Display the permit on the rear-view mirror whenever parked in an accessible space
documents: Application form including the medical professional referral section
Payment of the current fee listed by SPARC BC, unless hardship assistance applies
tips: The permit is yours, not the vehicle's. Use it in any car you drive or ride in.
Renew permanent permits online at online.sparc.bc.ca before they expire. Expired permits can't be renewed online.
Temporary permits can't be renewed. Send a new application if you still need one.
detail.time: 2 to 3 weeks from when your application is received

values.note: accessible parking placard; fee set by SPARC BC
